subject.title: feat: centralized filename encoding utility for multi-encoding Content-Disposition handling

question: Where should the shared multi-encoding filename decoder live, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/71517 be refreshed or replaced?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent boundary affects shared media code, bundled channel plugins, and plugin-facing reuse; automation should not choose that API direction without maintainer intent.

options.title: Use media-core or SDK boundary
options.body: Move the decoder into a plugin-safe shared surface and refresh or replace the candidate PR around that one helper.

options.title: Keep narrow channel repairs
options.body: Treat the current Feishu fixes as sufficient for now and defer non-Feishu multi-encoding cases until concrete channel reports arrive.

options.title: Require broader live repros first
options.body: Keep this issue open but ask for real non-Feishu channel failures before approving a shared utility.

recommendation.title: Use media-core or SDK boundary
recommendation.body: Move the decoder into a plugin-safe shared surface and refresh or replace the candidate PR around that one helper.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Feishu filename fixes and release/media-core-adjacent ownership make this the strongest available owner for the boundary decision.
